= Yubnub CLI — encryption & transport audit (2026-10-13) =

*The “Ghidra encryption check,” applied to the Yubnub CLI itself
(and cross-read against the APK findings in
`docs/zlibrary-apk-ghidra-research-2026-10-13.md` §8). Static audit
of `yubnub.html` + registry data; new tests pin the invariants.*

== Registry transport (the part that touches the network) ==

- 94 URL templates: **74 HTTPS**, 17 `local:` (in-app commands),
  **3 HTTP — `deli`, `tec`, `a9`, all D-flagged dead services**
  (del.icio.us 2017, Technorati 2016, A9 retired) kept as historical
  records. No *live* command resolves over cleartext.
- New test: “live templates are HTTPS-only (dead historical entries
  exempt)” — fails the build if a future live `http://` template
  lands. Second new test pins the legal book trio `guten`/`ia`/`ol`.
  Suite: **8/8 pass**; rebuilt `yubnub.xdc` 152,189 B,
  sha256 `138373c75c02351bf89161dcc9e8514e10d20b96f6fa327b9a272544d7eb14d6`.

== Engine posture ==

- No `eval(`, no WebSocket, no remote script/style fetches — the app
  is one self-contained file; command resolution is string-template
  substitution ending in `window.open` / fetch-free navigation.
- The `{…}` pipe evaluator and `${…}` shielding (the two historical
  engine bugs) mean *user-typed* braces are data, not code — there is
  no path from a typed command line to script execution beyond the
  registered template the user invoked.
- **Custom commands (`yubnub.custom`) persist in localStorage in
  plaintext** — the same plaintext-storage pattern flagged in Z-Lib
  sample A (21 plain SharedPreferences, no Keystore). On a single-user
  browser profile this is low-risk (any script running as the page
  already owns the data), and there is no credential material in a
  Yubnub template by design; noted, accepted, documented rather than
  “fixed” with fake crypto.

== webxdc transport ==

Inside Delta Chat, the `.xdc` is exchanged over the chat's
Autocrypt/OpenPGP end-to-end encryption — transport confidentiality
comes from the host messenger, not from the app, which correctly
implements none of its own. Status updates use the webxdc sendUpdate
channel; the app stores nothing server-side because there is no
server.

== Cross-read vs the APKs (why this audit exists) ==

The Ghidra/JADX pass set the bar the CLI was then measured against:
cipher inventory (A: AES/CBC, no ECB ✓), plaintext token storage
(A ✗ / CLI: plaintext-by-design, no tokens), TLS behaviour (A: one
empty `checkServerTrusted` flagged; CLI: inherits browser TLS with
HTTPS-only live templates ✓), and provenance (A/B signers vs the
CLI's deterministic, sha256-pinned, in-repo build — anyone can
rebuild `yubnub.xdc` and compare hashes, the property sample B's
impersonated test-key signature can never offer).
